origin: cwe/89/java Key Principles: MyBatis #{} binds values, while ${} performs raw text substitution and must be safe by construction for identifiers

finding.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
finding.sink_code: @Select("SELECT id, status, total_cents FROM invoices WHERE tenant_id = #{tenantId} ORDER BY ${sort}")
finding.summary: A request-controlled sort value flows through service code into MyBatis ${} text substitution in an ORDER BY clause.

trap: Replacing ${sort} with #{sort}, escaping the sort string, or focusing only on tenantId because it already uses #{}. MyBatis cannot bind an identifier as a value; sort must resolve to a fixed allowlisted SQL fragment before reaching ${}.
must_preserve: tenantId remains bound with #{tenantId}, the default created_at sort remains available, and legitimate sort choices still return InvoiceRow records without accepting arbitrary SQL fragments.
